title: Coordinate blowup lowers the branch number
statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a regular Noetherian affine scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $t_1,\ldots,t_m\in A$, with $m\geq1$, satisfy the following pointwise coordinate condition: at every point $u$ of $U$, those $t_j$ whose germs lie in the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ are distinct members of a regular system of parameters of that local ring. Such a system in a regular local ring of dimension $d$ means $d$ generators of its maximal ideal. Let $D_U=V(\prod_{j=1}^m t_j)$ and $M_U=V(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$ as closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $b:U^+=\operatorname{Bl}_{M_U}(U)	o U$ be the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Its standard affine charts, indexed by $1\leq i\leq m$, have coordinate rings $A_i=A[t_j/t_i:1\leq j\leq m,\ j
e i]\subseteq A[1/t_i]$. Write $t_i'=t_i$ and $t_j'=t_j/t_i$ for $j
e i$. On this chart the strict transform of $D_U$ [def-nagata-strict-transform] has equation $\prod_{j
e i}t_j'=0$. For every point $y\in\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, the local ring $(A_i)_y$ is regular; the germs of the factors $t_j'$ with $j
e i$ which vanish at $y$ extend to a regular system of parameters of $(A_i)_y$, and all the other factors are units there. Thus the strict-transform equation in this local ring is a unit times a product of distinct members of a regular system of parameters. The strict transform is empty or a normal crossings divisor, meaning a closed subscheme whose ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] and which etale locally has such an equation, and its number of geometric branches at $y$ equals $\#\{j
e i:t_j'\in y\}\leq m-1$. For $m=1$ the empty product is $1$ and the strict transform is empty. After every etale base change [def-weil-etale-morphism] the displayed chart equations remain valid for the base-changed blowup and strict transform, with the local-parameter assertion made in the local ring of each chosen point. No locality of $A$ or $A_i$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121, and the depth computation in 4.1.8, printed p. 118: local blowup charts and the strict-transform equation.

proof.text:
Put $I=(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$. By [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] and [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], the standard charts cover the blowup and have rings $C=A[I/t_i]=A[t_j/t_i:j
e i]\subset A[1/t_i]$. Write $a=t_i$, $z_j=t_j/t_i$ for $j
e i$, and $P=\prod_{j
e i}z_j$. The relations are $t_j=az_j$, and hence $f=\prod_jt_j=a^mP$. By [lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal], $IC=(a)$, so the complement of the center on this chart is $D(a)$. Each $C$ is finitely generated over the Noetherian ring $A$, and thus Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian].

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121; chart computation underlying 4.1.8, printed p. 118

proof.text:
Fix a prime $y\subset C$, put $p=y\cap A$, $R=A_p$ and $S=C_y$. Localizing the generators and their relations identifies $C\otimes_A R$ with $R[IR/a]\subset R[1/a]$, and $S$ with its localization at the prime induced by $y$: both maps send every ratio to $t_j/a$, and the inverse follows by inverting the elements of $A\setminus p$. If $p
ot\supset I$, choose $t_k
otin p$. The equation $t_k=az_k$ (or $t_k=a$ for $k=i$) forces $a
otin y$, and hence $a
otin p$. Thus $R[IR/a]=R$ and $S=R$. Each nonunit $z_j$ is then a unit multiple of $t_j$, and the pointwise hypothesis gives its extension to a regular system of parameters; multiplying selected parameter generators by units preserves their generating ideal. This proves regularity and the parameter assertion away from the center.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121; chart computation underlying 4.1.8, printed p. 118

proof.text: If $p\supset I$, all $t_1,\ldots,t_m$ belong to the maximal ideal of $R$ and are distinct members of a regular parameter system by hypothesis. Reorder and complete this list to $t_1,\ldots,t_d$. Apply [lem-trf-permissible-coordinate-chart] over this regular local ring, with its $r=m$, $J=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and chart index $i$. It says that the chart $R[IR/a]$ is regular and that at every point its vanishing exceptional coordinate $a$ and vanishing ratio coordinates $z_j$ occur among a regular system of parameters. Step 2 identifies its chosen local ring with $S$, so $S$ is regular and those exact germs, rather than coordinates in a purportedly local global chart, have the required parameter property. In particular $a$ and all nonunit $z_j$ occupy distinct positions in such a system.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121; chart computation underlying 4.1.8, printed p. 118

proof.text: By [def-nagata-strict-transform] the strict transform is the scheme-theoretic closure of the inverse image of $D_U$ away from the center. The preserved immersion is quasi-compact: on each of the finitely many standard affine charts its source is the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}((C/(f))[1/a])$; it is quasi-separated since it is an immersion. The scheme-theoretic image description [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] and its restriction to open charts [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] identify its chart ideal with $K=\ker(C\to(C/(f))[1/a])$. Explicitly $h\in K$ iff $a^nh\in(f)$ for some $n\ge0$. At $y$ this becomes $KS=\{h\in S:\exists n,\ a^nh\in fS\}$: clearing the localization denominators shows that $a^n h/s\in fS$ iff some $v\notin y$ satisfies $va^nh\in(f)$. Thus the closure is computed by saturation of $(f)$ by $a$, including all scheme structure.

source.place: Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform; affine sections supported on the exceptional divisor; morphisms.tex Tag 01R8, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image (1)-(3)

proof.text: We compute this saturation in $S$. Away from the center $a$ is a unit by Step 2, so $(f):a^\infty=(P)$. Over the center, Step 3 and [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] say that $S$ is a domain and that $a$ and the nonunit factors of $P$ are pairwise nonassociate prime elements. Nonassociation follows also from their distinct cotangent-basis positions. If $a^nh\in(a^mP)$, each such prime factor of $P$ divides $h$, since it does not divide $a$; unique factorization therefore gives $P\mid h$. Conversely $h=Pq$ satisfies $a^mh=fq$. Hence again $(f):a^\infty=(P)$. All stalks of the closure ideal thus agree with those of $(P)$, so the chart strict transform is exactly $V(P)$. When $m=1$, $P=1$ and this closed subscheme is empty.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121; chart computation underlying 4.1.8, printed p. 118

proof.text: Steps 2 and 3 prove the pointwise coordinate condition for the $m-1$ functions $z_j$ on the regular Noetherian chart $\operatorname{Spec}C$. In each local ring $P$ is a unit times the product of exactly the nonunit $z_j$. It is a nonzerodivisor, because that regular local ring is a domain by [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization]. A function whose multiplication is injective on all local rings has injective multiplication on the ring (a nonzero kernel element survives at some prime). Thus $V(P)$ is an effective Cartier divisor in the sense of [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], and the equations give normal crossings by [def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor]. For $m\ge2$, apply [lem-trf-nc-coordinate-max-stratum] with $s=m-1$ and functions $(z_j)_{j\ne i}$: its geometric-branch conclusion is exactly $\#\{j\ne i:z_j\in y\}\le m-1$. For $m=1$ the empty divisor has zero branches. In particular an ordinary parameter hyperplane is not being assumed geometrically irreducible without the cited geometric-branch theorem.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121; chart computation underlying 4.1.8, printed p. 118

proof.text: Let $v:W\to U$ be etale. Its flatness is part of [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The comparison of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] is an isomorphism by [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change]. On affine pieces $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset W$ it identifies the pullback of the $i$-chart with $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_A B)$, and the named ratios with the pulled-back ratios. Here $B$ is flat over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to $0\to K\to C\to(C/(f))[1/a]$: the kernel after tensoring with $B$ is the extended ideal $K(C\otimes_A B)$. Localization and quotient commute with this tensor product by their defining universal properties. Thus the kernel is precisely the closure kernel for the base-changed product divisor, and Step 5 identifies it with the ideal generated by the pulled-back $P$. This proves the scheme-theoretic strict-transform formula after base change without a hypothesis about generic points.

source.place: Tag 0805, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up; Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform; algebra.tex Tag 00HD, lemma-flat

proof.text: The projection $W\times_UU^+\to U^+$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. On any affine subchart $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ its ring map is etale and finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine]; $E$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. For a chosen prime $q\subset E$ over $y$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-prime-generates-maximal] says that the images of any parameter system of $C_y$ generate the maximal ideal of $E_q$, and [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension] says the two dimensions are equal. These images are consequently a regular system of parameters of $E_q$ by [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. A local homomorphism preserves whether a germ is a unit, so the same subset of the $z_j$ vanishes, and the parameter assertion holds at each chosen point. The branch interpretation and its invariance are then exactly [lem-trf-nc-coordinate-max-stratum] for $m\ge2$, with the already empty $m=1$ case handled by Step 5.
